title: work.py: what the work does when a chain ends (usage limits first)
about: Task W132 (stop at a usage limit) on top of the work. A work starts work chains, one task each, on a session budget. Each tick it judges the chains that ended: work_decide turns a chain's stop cause into run, hold, stop, raise or pend. A usage limit is the one cause the work waits out and retries; stop_on_limit ends the work there instead.

each new chain's cap is what is left after live chains' caps, divided by the slots still to fill (rounded down, at least 1): 20 left and 3 free gives 6, 7, 7

writes the cap file of each live chain work_off just dropped, lowered to the run it is on, so it ends after that run; nothing judges it, so it is outside this work's budget and slots, and a later work counts it as a chain it did not start (work_foreign) until it ends
a daemon thread every 300 s; skipped while the last is still running
stop action (a limit with stop_on_limit, or a cause only a person can judge) → the whole work ends
idle, or a blocked or capped chain that moved nothing (not done) → a raise on that item; the other tasks go on if the raise succeeds
the raise cannot be written, or next_item still names the item → the work ends
the work ending drops every chain from work_chains, then each live one is told to end after the run it is on
a chain still not on the box after 15 s → the work ends, with console.log's cause
start_chain returns None → the work ends; chains already started are told to end, except one started in this same tick that dfs_runs cannot see yet

a chain whose cap file cannot be written is returned in a list; only stopping by hand (work_end_chain) reads it and names the first; every automatic work_off drops the list, so that chain keeps running to its old cap and nobody is told
a pull request that cannot be read is an event line; the work goes on
console.log unreadable (OSError) → chain_cause returns '', so work_off's reason carries no cause and nobody is told
a task that ended on its cap, or was held by a limit, goes to the front next time
in order: the pin, each carried task still workable, then the roadmap's next item
as many as there are free slots; a task that would share the one checkout with a running chain is passed over
nothing workable → the work stays on and asks again each tick; nothing is spent
during a hold nothing new starts, but chains that ended are still judged
